title: How Lovely Are Thy Dwellings, Lord
description: How Lovely Are Thy Dwellings, Lord in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Milton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 914 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Blessedness of the Devout”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How love-ly are thy dwel-lings, Lord, From noise and trou-ble free; How beau-ti-ful the sweet ac-cord Of souls that pray to thee.

lines: How lovely are thy dwellings, Lord,
From noise and trouble free;
How beautiful the sweet accord
Of souls that pray to thee.
Lord God of hosts, that reign'st on high,
They are the truly blest,
Who only will on thee rely,
In thee alone will rest.
They pass refreshed the thirsty vale,
The dry and barren ground,
As through a fruitful, watery dale,
Where springs and showers abound.
They journey on from strength to strength,
With joy and gladsome cheer,
Till all before our God at length.
In Zion do appear.
For God, the Lord, both sun and shield,
Gives grace and glory bright;
No good from him shall be withheld
Whose ways are just and right.

licence: Public domain: John Milton died in 1674.
credits: Words by John Milton (1608–1674), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
